findings.finding: Self-normalized Equation 2 is cited as PDF p. 3, but appears on PDF p. 2.

findings.finding: Nested-support assumptions allow a base draw outside an intermediate support, making a later density ratio 0/0 unless a zero-weight path convention is stated. The raw product as written is not defined for every allowed case.
findings.evidence: AIS PDF p. 4 permits nested support; PDF p. 5 Equations 4–5 define the raw path/product and Equations 6–10 give the extended-space law. Curator counterexample f0=f1=(1,0), f2=(1,1), T1=identity satisfies the stated support and invariance assumptions. With base state 1 (probability 1/2), the first ratio f1/f2 is 0, and the next ratio f0/f1 is 0/0.
findings.recommended_fix: On the first zero numerator, assign the run zero weight and stop subsequent ratio and endpoint evaluation; the run contributes zero to both weighted numerator and denominator. Preserve the all-weights-zero undefined-estimate warning, and add an exact finite guard case. Alternatively restrict the maintained raw formula to strictly positive densities.
findings.root_preferred_resolution_assessed: Explicit zero-weight termination is valid; no objection.

findings.finding: The correction that x_j follows T_(j+1) needs its upper-index exception: x_(n−1) is drawn directly from p_n, and T_n is not part of Equation 4.
findings.evidence: AIS PDF p. 5, Equation 4 visually inspected. Source PDF p. 6 intermediate-state paragraph has T_(j−1), which is indeed inconsistent with the main sequence. For 0<=j<=n−2 the actual preceding transition is T_(j+1); the highest state is the initial base draw.
findings.recommended_fix: Qualify T_(j+1) to j<=n−2, and explicitly state that x_(n−1) is drawn directly from p_n.

verified_mathematical_points: AIS main state indexing and successive-weight formula agree with PDF p. 5 Equations 4–5.
AIS invariance rather than reversibility/ergodicity suffices for intermediate kernels; the reverse kernels in the extended-space proof need not be simulated.

AIS weighted-mass and normalizing-ratio identities, finite-sample self-normalized bias, and unweighted-endpoint distinction are consistent with the proof and exact finite examples, subject to resolving zero-weight path handling.
AIS terminal fixed-length average and dependence caveats agree with PDF pp. 6 and 8.
TT mutual reversal, outward/return indexing, full-path acceptance, rejection retention, 2n kernel applications and independent density-scale cancellation agree with PDF pp. 5–7 Equations 5–12.
TT invariant-but-not-mutually-reversed cycle counterexample and correct-reversal identity-transition example match exact calculations.

Later TT normalizer estimate is correctly separated from the 1994 transition identity; AIS PDF pp. 19–20 Equations 28–29 use accepted and rejected transitions and discuss autocorrelation and variance.

ais.scope: Finite exact laws and counterexamples only. No continuous-state theorem certification, variance bound, benchmark replication, author implementation, paid provider or training.

tempered.scope: Exact finite path enumeration, including rejection self-loops. No author-code or benchmark replication, universal efficiency bound, guarantee of ergodicity or numerical implementation audit.

test_execution: Both supplied calculator programs ran successfully; their exact Fraction-based assertions passed (192 AIS finite family cases and 72 TT finite family cases). The additional two-state nested-support zero/zero case was executed separately and exhibited the stated ZeroDivisionError, with the guarded mean 1/2 matching Z0/Z2.
overall: Core positive-density formulas and supplied finite arithmetic pass this bounded supporting audit. Four actionable curation/locator findings were reported; no repository changes were made.
